sections.title: First greetings and Swedish sounds
body: Use whole chunks first: Hej! · Jag heter … · Trevligt att träffas. · Hej då!
Hej is neutral in most everyday meetings. Tjena is more casual.
At A0, understand the purpose in English, then repeat the Swedish aloud.

sections.title: Nine vowels and sound length
body: Swedish has nine vowel letters: a, e, i, o, u, y, å, ä and ö. Listen before using English sound approximations.
A stressed vowel is often long before one consonant, but short before two: tak (roof) versus tack (thanks).
Swedish stress is not always initial. Copy the model rhythm and aim for clear contrasts.

assignment.title: Episode 1 mission: First greetings and Swedish sounds
assignment.instructions:
LISTEN: Hear the audio twice and answer: What is the speaker's name?

READ: Read once for purpose and once for detail. Answer: What is this notice for?

SPEAK: Greet a classmate, say your name, and close. Try once without the model, then repeat more clearly.

WRITE: Write a two-line greeting and introduction. Check word order and spelling.

TRANSFER: Use God morgon instead of Hej and choose another name.

RETURN: Greet and introduce yourself from memory.
assignment.model:
Speaking: Hej! Jag heter Alex. Trevligt att träffas. Hej då!
Writing: Hej!
Jag heter Alex.
